facts.statement: Platypelta lived during the early Late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 77.5 to 76.5 million years ago, in southern Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: It is known from the Late Cretaceous Dinosaur Park Formation (early Late Campanian stage, about 77.5-76.5 Ma ago) of southern Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: In 2018, Penkalski named the genus Platypelta for specimens AMNH 5337 and AMNH 5403 after finding them distinct from Euoplocephalus tutus in cladistic analysis.
facts.quote: In 2018, Penkalski published a study containing a cladistic analyses of such forms. In it, AMNH 5337 and AMNH 5403 were recovered in a joint different position from Euoplocephalus tutus specimens CMN 210, UALVP 31, and AMNH 5406. He named a separate genus for AMNH 5337 and AMNH 5403: Platypelta, with as type species Platypelta coombsi.

facts.statement: The generic name Platypelta comes from Greek words meaning "wide" and "small shield," referring to the animal's broad osteoderms.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek platys, "wide", and plate, "small shield", in reference to the broad osteoderms.

facts.statement: The species name coombsi honors Walter P. Coombs Jr., a pioneer in the study of ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Walter P. Coombs Jr., who pioneered the study of ankylosaurs in the late twentieth century.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen AMNH 5337 was found at an altitude of 667 meters, indicating an age of about 76.8 million years.
facts.quote: The holotype, AMNH 5337, was found in a layer of the Dinosaur Park Formation at an altitude of 667 metres, which indicates an age of about 76,8 million years.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton includes the skull but lacks the tail and hindlimbs, and shows signs of being a mature, aged individual such as fused ribs and a fused shoulder girdle.
facts.quote: It consists of a skeleton with skull, lacking the tail and hindlimbs. It represents a mature and aged individual, in view of fused ribs, a fused shoulder girdle, rough articulation surfaces and rough armour.

facts.statement: In 2018, the estimated length of Platypelta was six meters.
facts.quote: In 2018, its length was estimated at six metres.

facts.statement: The foot is robust and equipped with arched claws.
facts.quote: The foot is robust with arched claws.

facts.statement: Platypelta is a member of the clade Euoplocephalini, which Penkalski established as an approximate synonym of Ankylosaurini.
facts.quote: More precisely, it was a member of the clade Euoplocephalini, established by Penkalski, which is an approximate synonym of Ankylosaurini in several studies.

facts.statement: In the evolutionary tree, Platypelta is placed above Scolosaurus and below Dyoplosaurus.
facts.quote: In the evolutionary tree it was placed above Scolosaurus and below Dyoplosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2013, Arbour and Currie suggested that AMNH 5337 and AMNH 5403 belong to Euoplocephalus, proposing that differences might result from growth and development changes.
facts.quote: In 2013, Victoria Megan Arbour and Philip Currie continued to refer AMNH 5337 (and AMNH 5403) to Euoplocephalus, suggesting that differences from other skulls referred to Euoplocephalus could be due to changes occurring with growth and development.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen AMNH 5337 was excavated in 1914 by Barnum Brown and Peter Kaisen in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: En 1914, Barnum Brown y Peter Kaisen , trabajando para el Museo Americano de Historia Natural, en Alberta, en Sand Creek, cerca del río Red Deer, a unos 13 kilómetros al sudeste de Steveville, excavaron un esqueleto de anquilosaurio, espécimen AMNH 5337.

facts.statement: In 2018, Paul Penkalski established the genus Platypelta based on cladistic analysis showing AMNH 5337 and AMNH 5403 formed a distinct group separate from Euoplocephalus tutus.
facts.quote: En 2018, Penkalski publicó un estudio que contiene un análisis cladístico de tales formas. En él se recuperaron AMNH 5337 y AMNH 5403 en una posición conjunta diferente de las muestras de Euoplocephalus tutus CMN 210, UALVP 31 y AMNH 5406.

facts.statement: The generic name Platypelta means "wide shield" in Greek, referring to the animal's broad osteoderms.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del griego platys , "ancho", y la pelta, "escudo", en referencia a los osteodermos amplios.

facts.statement: The holotype AMNH 5337 was found in the Dinosaur Park Formation at an altitude of 667 meters, dating to approximately 76.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo, AMNH 5337, se encontró en una capa de la Formación Dinosaur Park a una altitud de 667 metros, que indica una edad de aproximadamente 76,8 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype represents a mature, elderly individual, evidenced by fused ribs, fused shoulder girdle, rough joint surfaces, and rough armor.
facts.quote: Representa a un individuo maduro y anciano, a la vista de las costillas fusionadas, la cintura escapular fusionada, las superficies de articulación rugosa y la armadura áspera.

facts.statement: Specimen ROM 813 is a skullless skeleton containing the complete hindquarters, forelimbs, and hindlimbs, preserving skin impressions alongside numerous osteoderms.
facts.quote: ROM 813 es un esqueleto que carece del cráneo pero que contiene la grupa completa, extremidades anteriores y extremidades posteriores. Además de una gran cantidad de osteodermos, conserva las impresiones cutáneas.

facts.statement: Platypelta is classified within the family Ankylosauridae, subfamily Ankylosaurinae, and tribe Ankylosaurini.
facts.quote: Platypelta fue colocada en 2018, dentro de los Ankylosauridae, más específicamente en Ankylosaurinae como miembro de la tribu Ankylosaurini.

facts.statement: Platypelta lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Platypelta is the tribe Euoplocephalini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Euoplocephalini

facts.statement: Platypelta belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
